column3: Good evening to you, my lady. I am the hitsuji doshin, a member of a Far Eastern delegation come to share our traditions of Heavensturn with the good people of Eorzea. If there is aught you would know of this year's celebration, you need only ask.

At the turning of the year, a small delegation of our people will journey to Eorzea to celebrate the coming of Heavensturn, and in so doing, strengthen the bonds of friendship between Eorzea and the Far East.
Under the guidance of our leader, the hitsuji bugyo, we wish to celebrate the year of the sheep by blessing the people of Limsa Lominsa with pleasant dreams.
We are most grateful for your continued assistance with this year's festivities.
Should you wish to draw omikuji, the omikujishi will be offering his services for the remainder of the celebration.

You are unfamiliar with this festival? The tradition has a rich history which dates back centuries, but I do not wish to bore you, so I shall try and keep my summation brief.

Heavensturn is a celebration that marks the start of a new year, though the way in which it is observed differs from region to region. Here in Eorzea, it is said that the Twelve select one among them to keep vigil over the realm until the next passing of the twelve moons. I believe this year it is Menphina, the goddess of love, who has been charged with this duty.
In the Far East, however, the changing of the year is heralded by one of twelve totem animals. As you have no doubt discerned from my helm, this year we pay homage to the magnificent hitsuji.
I speak of the creature you know as a “sheep,” which we likewise consider to be a symbol of sound sleep.
